data.body:
adopt tracks only stamped markdown blocks. Record every artifact: marked block in a file, JSON/TOML key in an MCP or settings file, hook entry, plugin or command or skill or subagent file, git hook, env line, worktree dir. Stored as an event agent.onboarded {agent, artifacts[]} (project-visible) plus a machine-local file for user-scope paths; digests detect later edits. Existing installs are reconstructed once by scanning the descriptor's paths, marked 'reconstructed'. This is what makes offboarding exact.

NOTE 2026-11-05 (D-manifest-write-time): this item is now the HELPER only; where it differs from the text above, this note governs. Deliver: one shared record call taking agent, path, artifact kind (marked block, JSON or TOML key, hook entry, plugin, command, skill or subagent file, git hook, env line, worktree dir), region or key, digest, descriptor and ddflow version; re-recording the same path and key updates the digest, so a rewrite through upgrade stays true; project paths reach the log as agent.onboarded {agent, artifacts[]}, one event per run rather than one per file; user-scope paths go to the machine-local file; a read that returns an agent's artifacts and says which digests changed. No writer is instrumented here: P-agent-lifecycle.manifest-adopt, -hooks, -mcp and -githooks do that, -reconstruct handles existing installs. The record call must serve a writer in another module with no change here: P-agent-parity.permissions, P-agent-parity.kilo-plugin, DSH-overlay and OB-emit-manifest only call it. Globs: event kinds register as data since SE-event-registry, so core/events.py is not needed (3c72376ce added a kind without it); the old ddflow/services/adopt.py glob named a file f474937c4 split into a package, and it moves to -adopt.
data.title: Install manifest helper: the one shared call every onboarding writer records through (path, kind, region or key, digest, descriptor and ddflow version), agent.onboarded and the machine-local file

data.body: D-manifest-write-time. Instrument the writers in ddflow/services/adopt/ (_upsert._upsert_block, _native._write_native_rule, _commands._write_harness_files and _write_command, _docs._write_driver) with the shared record call. An MCP registration made from _launch is recorded inside mcpconfig (manifest-mcp), a hook entry from _commands._install_prompt_hooks inside claudehooks (manifest-hooks): do not record them twice. Project scaffolding in .ddflow/ is not per-agent and is not recorded. Tests: each writer's artifact is recorded with the right kind, region and digest; a second adopt leaves one entry per artifact; a dry run records nothing.
data.title: Adopt records what it writes through the manifest helper: marked blocks, native rule files, command, skill and subagent files, drivers

data.body: D-manifest-write-time. Instrument install for every hook style (claudehooks.install_spec and the ddflow/services/hookwriters modules) so each hook entry is recorded as a hook entry in its file, keyed by event and marker, never the whole settings file: foreign hooks in the same file stay unowned. Uninstall drops the entry from the manifest. Tests: one style per writer module, a foreign hook beside ours is not recorded, install then uninstall leaves no entry.
data.title: Agent hook writers record each hook entry through the manifest helper

data.body: D-manifest-write-time. Instrument mcpconfig.register, _register_toml and _register_cordis, and harness.enable_project_servers (a settings key), recording the exact key owned, not the file. A user-scope config goes to the machine-local file through the helper, never into the committed log. Tests: JSON and TOML shapes, a user-scope path stays out of the event, a foreign server in the same file is not recorded, a repeated register leaves one entry.
data.title: MCP registration records each JSON or TOML key it writes through the manifest helper, user-scope paths included

data.body: D-manifest-write-time. These are project artifacts, not one agent's: record them under a project owner, which offboard --project removes. Instrument enforce/hooks._install_one, the pre-commit stage entry and the .gitattributes lines mergedrivers writes. The lane hooks in ddflow/services/swarm/ (githook, lanehooks) live in a lane's worktree and go with it: out of scope. Tests: install and uninstall each, a foreign hook or a user's .gitattributes line is not recorded.
data.title: Project git hooks, the pre-commit entry and .gitattributes merge-driver lines are recorded through the manifest helper

data.body: D-manifest-write-time rejected a scan as the way to record NEW writes, because it cannot tell ddflow's writes from the user's; it stays only for installs made before the helper existed. Every entry is marked 'reconstructed', so offboard can treat it as less certain than a recorded write, and a later recorded write replaces it. Runs once per project and is idempotent. What triggers the run is not settled: decide it at the research gate and widen the globs then. Tests: a project with ddflow files and no manifest, a second run changes nothing, a recorded entry is never downgraded.
data.title: Existing installs enter the manifest once, by scanning each descriptor's paths, marked 'reconstructed'
